sentences.en: just describe in English sentences or, insert whatever language you speak, a native language, you know, just normal conversational text to a computer and have it do what you want.
sentences.zh: ——或者不管你说什么语言，母语——你知道的，就像用平常的日常对话文本跟计算机交流，让它做你想做的事。

sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，你知道的，还有什么比它直接就是你的操作系统更亲民的呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you turn on the computer and BASIC starts, you know?
sentences.zh: 比如，你打开电脑，BASIC就启动了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so that was the way, you know, Commodore 64s, TRS 80s, Apple IIs, right?
sentences.zh: 对，所以当时的方式，你知道的，Commodore 64、TRS 80、Apple II，对吧？

sentences.zh: 它们一开机就直接进入BASIC解释器。

sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it worked well for that because you could say things like, it wasn't print def or see out or what are these things?
sentences.zh: 而且这种方式效果很好，因为你可以说一些话，它不是print def或者cout或者这些乱七八糟的？

sentences.en: It was like, print.
sentences.zh: 它就是，print。

sentences.en: And then you just gave it, you know, this thing you wanted it to print.
sentences.zh: 然后你直接把你想打印的东西传给它。

sentences.en: And then the next line, so you say, print hello world.
sentences.zh: 接下来的一行，比如你说，print hello world。

sentences.en: And the next line, go to previous line, right?
sentences.zh: 然后下一行，回到上一行，对吧？

sentences.en: Go to 10.
sentences.zh: 转到 10。

sentences.en: 10, print hello world.
sentences.zh: 10，打印 hello world。

sentences.zh: 20，go to 10，对吧？

sentences.zh: 你知道的，对，如果你仔细想想，go to语句就是……

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你总听到各种说法，比如go to是万恶之源之类的话。

sentences.en: And then somebody proved that, you know, this wasn't a hard proof or anything, but that you could basically, like, if you use for loops and breaks and returns, you can, like,
sentences.zh: 然后有人证明了，你知道，这倒不是什么严谨的证明，但大意是如果你使用for循环、break和return，你基本上就可以

sentences.zh: 把任何包含go to的程序转换成用for循环和break实现的程序，对吧？

sentences.zh: 所以，go to并不是必需的。

sentences.en: But there's, like, appeal to it.
sentences.zh: 但它确实有某种吸引力。

sentences.en: You know, the idea that, like, I'm going to label this line as, like, line 8 and then somewhere else, like, go to 8.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种想法，就是“我把这一行标为第8行，然后在其他地方写个go to 8”。

sentences.en: Like, it's so much more intuitive than, like, a for loop where you have to, like, count up and each time this i has a different value.
sentences.zh: 这比那种你得向上计数、每次这个i都有不同值的for循环要直观太多了。

sentences.en: And, you know, it might not be the most useful, but for someone who's just starting out, it makes more sense.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它可能不是最有用的，但对刚入门的人来说，它更容易理解。

sentences.en: Like, they look at that and they know immediately what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他们一看就知道是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is true.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the for loop concept takes a while to get around.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，for循环的概念确实需要花点时间才能理解。

sentences.en: You just kind of have to get to that epiphany stage.
sentences.zh: 你必须达到那种醍醐灌顶的阶段。

sentences.en: Like, oh, I get it now.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我现在懂了。

sentences.en: And, I mean, the whole issue that us programmers understand is you need to be able to be very precise to the, and actually saying go to this line.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们程序员都明白的一个问题是，你需要非常精确地指定到某一行，并真正说出“跳转到这一行”。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, like, very, if you say return, it's, like, return to what?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常……如果你说return，这就变成了“返回到哪里去？”

sentences.en: And early basic didn't have functions or procedures.
sentences.zh: 早期的basic没有函数或过程。

sentences.en: It was just, you know, straight down the line, imperative programming, just, you know, line after line.
sentences.zh: 它只是，你知道的，从头到尾的指令式编程，也就是，一行接一行。

sentences.zh: 我们应该提一下，我们这里不讨论Visual Basic。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 我们继续。

sentences.zh: 所以，像第一代的basic，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, there was, you had to have every number line.
sentences.zh: 比如，每一行都必须有行号。

sentences.en: You know, there weren't procedures.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时没有过程。

sentences.en: You could do these go-tos and you could have, you know, kind of Boolean statements or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你可以用这些go to，还可以有一些布尔表达式之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, for people who don't know, the way the computer, and Patrick will probably know a lot better than I will, so I'll let him correct me.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于不太了解的人来说，计算机的工作方式——帕特里克可能比我清楚得多，所以我让他来纠正我。

sentences.en: But the way I understand it is you have a program counter.
sentences.zh: 但我的理解是，你有一个程序计数器。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you have a multi-threaded...
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果你有一个多线程的……

sentences.en: The CPU has a program counter.
sentences.zh: CPU有一个程序计数器。

sentences.en: The CPU has a program counter for each thread, right, which says, like, what instruction that thread is on.
sentences.zh: CPU为每个线程都有一个程序计数器，对吧，它指示该线程当前执行到哪条指令。

sentences.en: Or in the case of basic, you just have one, which is for your thread.
sentences.zh: 或者在basic的情况下，你只有一个，就是为你自己的线程服务的。

sentences.en: And so it just, the program counter keeps stepping through until it encounters, like, a branch.
sentences.zh: 所以它只是不断地推进程序计数器，直到遇到分支指令。

sentences.en: So a branch might be, you know, an if statement.
sentences.zh: 所以分支可能是一个if语句。

sentences.en: So if something is true, then you're going to go to the next program counter.
sentences.zh: 如果某个条件为真，你就会跳到下一个程序计数器。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you're going to skip all the way down to the end of that if block, right?
sentences.zh: 否则，你就会一直跳到那个if代码块的末尾，对吧？

sentences.en: Or a go-to is an explicit branch.
sentences.zh: 或者go to就是一个显式分支。

sentences.en: You're actually saying, you know, take the program counter and set it to this other instruction.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在说，把程序计数器设置为另一条指令。

sentences.en: Well, in basic, it makes that, like, very explicit.
sentences.zh: 而在basic中，这一点表现得非常明显。

sentences.en: Like, in the first version of basic, you literally wrote the program counter for all of your instructions.
sentences.zh: 比如在第一版basic中，你实际上是为所有的指令亲手编写程序计数器。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, so you write the memory location, essentially, is what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以你基本上是在编写内存地址。

sentences.en: So we say 10, and that's, like, a line number, because line numbers don't have to be sequential.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说10，那就像是一个行号，因为行号不一定非得是连续的。

sentences.en: But you're essentially kind of stating, like, this is an abstracted version of memory.
sentences.zh: 但你本质上是在声明，这是一种抽象的内存版本。

sentences.en: So the processor would just execute the first memory instruction, then go to the next one, and go to the next one.
sentences.zh: 因此处理器会执行第一条内存指令，然后去下一条，再下一条。

sentences.en: Until I encounter, like you said, one of these things which said, affect the program counter in this way.
sentences.zh: 直到遇到像你说的那些会以这种方式影响程序计数器的指令。

sentences.en: Change it to this, or, you know, minus one, or plus one, or whatever, you know.
sentences.zh: 把它改成这样，或者，减一，或者加一，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so basic, yeah, you had to put the line numbers there so you knew where you were.
sentences.zh: 所以basic，对，你必须把行号写在那里，这样你才知道自己在哪。

sentences.en: And they had to be increasing so that you would, you know, keep moving forward in the memory and going up, unless you, you know, did a go-to.
sentences.zh: 而且它们必须是递增的，这样你才能在内存中继续向前推进、往上走，除非你执行了go to。

sentences.en: And then the second generation, you know, oh, we should say that Microsoft got its start in creating a version of basic.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二代，哦，我们应该说微软就是靠开发某个版本的basic起家的。

sentences.en: And that's kind of where they started.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们发迹的地方。

sentences.en: So we won't get into that large history.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就不深入讲那段庞大的历史了。

sentences.en: I don't know if this is still true, but the last time I checked, which was XP, it actually has QBasic in it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这现在是不是还这样，但我最后一次查的时候是在XP系统上，它里面其实自带了QBasic。

sentences.en: Like if you just scan your whole computer for QBasic.exe.
sentences.zh: 比如你在整台电脑上搜索QBasic.exe。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know anything about Vista or 7, but I know like 98 and XP in these 2000 actually had QBasic.
sentences.zh: 现在，我对Vista或7一无所知，但我知道98、XP和2000这些系统确实带有QBasic。

sentences.en: And they actually, in the same directory, there is a bananas.bas, and it's a game where you're like a monkey, and you have to throw a banana.
sentences.zh: 而且在同一个目录下，有一个叫bananas.bas的文件，那是一个游戏，扮演一只猴子，你得扔香蕉。

sentences.en: So it's a game right in QBasic.
sentences.zh: 所以这直接就是一个用QBasic写的小游戏。

sentences.en: I don't believe you.
sentences.zh: 我不信。

sentences.en: I'm going to go try that.
sentences.zh: 我要去试一下。

sentences.en: I'm going to go try this right now.
sentences.zh: 我马上就去试试。

sentences.en: So that was the first generation of basic.
sentences.zh: 所以那是第一代的basic。

sentences.en: And then the second generation came out, and, you know, this is quick, basic, like you're talking about QBasic.
sentences.zh: 然后第二代问世了，你知道的，这就是QuickBasic，就像你说的QBasic。

sentences.en: This is where this came out.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的来历。

sentences.en: And these, you didn't have to put line numbers if you didn't want.
sentences.zh: 在这些版本里，如果你不想的话，就不用写行号了。

sentences.en: You could have more like just labels as opposed to line numbers.
sentences.zh: 你可以用类似于标签的东西来代替行号。

sentences.en: And then you could actually have procedures.
sentences.zh: 并且你实际上还可以有过程。

sentences.en: So essentially functions.
sentences.zh: 也就是本质上的函数。

sentences.en: You could go to a function.
sentences.zh: 你可以跳转到一个函数。

sentences.en: And then like we said, that notion of return from a function is kind of vague.
sentences.zh: 而且就像我们说的，函数返回这个概念其实挺模糊的。

sentences.en: Like where are you returning to?
sentences.zh: 比如说，你到底是返回到哪里？

sentences.en: Well, it depends on where you came from.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于你是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: So when you say go to, you're going to a line.
sentences.zh: 所以当你使用跳转指令（go to）时，你是跳到某一行。

sentences.en: And then you have to later, you say go to some other line.
sentences.zh: 然后过一会儿，你又跳到其他某一行。

sentences.en: Like it's not just like the return is go to something that was stored previously, and that's the stack.
sentences.zh: 这就不仅仅是说，返回操作只是跳转到之前存储的某个位置，这就是栈的作用。

sentences.en: So the stack will store.
sentences.zh: 所以栈会把这些存储起来。

sentences.en: Have we talked about stack?
sentences.zh: 我们聊过栈吗？

sentences.en: No, I don't think we have.
sentences.zh: 没有，我觉得没有。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Why don't you cover it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不讲讲？

sentences.en: I think you'd be an expert on this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你在这方面绝对是个专家。

sentences.en: So for people who don't know, Patrick majored in computer engineering, and I majored in computer science.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于不太了解的观众，帕特里克主修计算机工程，而我主修计算机科学。

sentences.en: And then that alone makes him like much more applied and know things which are useful.
sentences.zh: 光是这一点，就让他显得实操性强得多，懂的也都是很有用的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, no crazy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，没那么夸张。

sentences.en: I think we're overstating this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们有点夸大其词了。

sentences.en: But then like on top of that, I did all theory.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我学的东西全都是理论。

sentences.en: Like I tried to stay away from all of the like databases and networking.
sentences.zh: 比如我尽量远离所有数据库和网络方面的东西。

sentences.en: And so that makes me even more, even like less useful when it comes like close to the metal stuff.
sentences.zh: 这让我变得更加……甚至在涉及底层硬件相关的东西时，显得更没用了。

sentences.en: So Patrick, why don't you explain stacks?
sentences.zh: 所以帕特里克，你来解释一下什么是栈吧？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So a stack is a data structure, but also it's something that is represented in the hardware in CPUs.
sentences.zh: 栈是一种数据结构，但它同时也体现在CPU的硬件之中。

sentences.en: And it is what's called a last in first out data structure.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“后进先出”（Last In, First Out）的数据结构。

sentences.en: So this implies that the last piece of data that you gave to the data structure, when you go to get something from it, it'll be the first thing that comes out.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着，你最后塞给这个数据结构的数据，当你去取的时候，会是第一个出来的东西。

sentences.en: So think of it as like, it's called a stack.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以把它想象成……正因它叫“栈”。

sentences.en: It's like a stack of papers.
sentences.zh: 就像一叠纸一样。

sentences.en: If you put one paper down, then put another on top and another on top,
sentences.zh: 如果你放下第一张纸，再把另一张叠在上面，又放一张在上面，

sentences.en: when you go to pull that last one, to pull the one on top, it's the most recent one you put there.
sentences.zh: 当你去拿最后那张、也就是最上面的那张时，它就是你最近才放上去的那张。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So if you think about functions, that's the way it works.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你思考一下函数，它的运作方式就是这样的。

sentences.en: So if I have function A calls function B calls function C, when I return from C, I want to go back to B.
sentences.zh: 如果我有函数A调用了函数B，函数B又调用了函数C，当我从C返回时，我想回到B。

sentences.en: And then when I return from B, I want to go back to A.
sentences.zh: 然后当我从B返回时，我想回到A。

sentences.en: So I want to go in the reverse order that I just came.
sentences.zh: 所以我想按照我来时的相反顺序回去。

sentences.en: And so that's what this return does.
sentences.zh: 这就是“返回”这个操作所做的事情。

sentences.en: So you need somewhere to stick this address of where you came from, the stack, yeah, the pointer, the program counter of where you came from.
sentences.zh: 因此，你需要一个地方来存放你来自哪里的地址——也就是栈，对，就是指针、记录你来路的程序计数器。

sentences.en: So you stick it on one of these stack structures, and then you go to your other function.
sentences.zh: 所以你把它塞进其中一个栈结构里，然后跳转到你的另一个函数。

sentences.en: And then when that function finishes, or calls another function, but when it finishes and returns, it takes the thing on the stack and goes, jumps to that location.
sentences.zh: 接着当那个函数执行完，或者调用了别的函数，但当它最终执行完毕并返回时，它会取出栈顶的那个东西，然后跳转到那个位置。

sentences.en: And hopefully, if everything worked out right and nothing bad had happened, you'll go back to where you left.
sentences.zh: 如果一切顺利、没有发生任何意外的话，你就会回到你离开的地方。

sentences.en: So if you were in function A and you called function B, it did its magic, and then returned, then you'll be back one line past the line where you called function B and function A.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在函数A中调用了函数B，B完成了它的魔术般的操作并返回，那么你就会回到函数A中调用函数B那行代码的下一行。

sentences.en: So that line plus one.
sentences.zh: 也就是那一行加一。

sentences.en: And that's also how things get passed to functions.
sentences.zh: 这也是数据传递给函数的方式。

sentences.en: So you also stick the things, the parameters you're calling the function with, you stick them on the stack, and they get popped back off too.
sentences.zh: 所以你还会把东西——也就是你调用函数时所用的参数——塞进栈里，它们随后也会被弹出（popped off）。

sentences.en: And that's how things get returned as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是返回值传递的方式。

sentences.en: So you can get the results of the function, as it were.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能获取函数的执行结果了，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: And so that's what the second generation did of BASIC was add these procedures and allow for procedural programming, which comes before object-oriented programming,
sentences.zh: 这就是第二代BASIC所做的事情：它添加了过程（procedures），并允许进行过程化编程，这在面向对象编程之前就有了，

sentences.en: which is what the third generation attempted to do.
sentences.zh: 而面向对象编程正是第三代语言试图去做的事情。

sentences.en: And that's where you get things like Visual Basic, so VBScript, which is a way to script Microsoft products, maybe others as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是你接触到Visual Basic、VBScript之类东西的源头，这是一种用来编写微软产品脚本的语言，或许也适用于其他产品。

sentences.en: I don't know the licensing agreements there.
sentences.zh: 我不太清楚那里的许可协议。

sentences.en: And like VisualBasic.net and these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 还有像VisualBasic.net以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: They tried to introduce the notions of object-oriented programming to BASIC, but we're not really going to talk about those today.
sentences.zh: 它们试图将面向对象编程的概念引入BASIC，但我们今天不打算深入讨论这些。

sentences.en: This is a nostalgia trip.
sentences.zh: 这是一次情怀之旅。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是。

sentences.en: I mean, VBS.net has all sorts of awesome stuff in it, and we'll cover it in another show.
sentences.zh: 我是说，VBS.net里有各种各样牛逼的东西，我们会在另一期节目里介绍它。

sentences.en: But today we're going to just focus on BASIC.
sentences.zh: 但今天我们只专注于BASIC。

sentences.en: So, you know, we both had experiences doing this, and we, you know, it's one of the things that I consider programming in BASIC to not have been really programming.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们俩都有过这段经历，而且，你知道的，这是我觉得在BASIC里编程甚至都算不上真正编程的一点。

sentences.en: You know, it was, and it is, but I fooled around with various, you know, like I said, the print, oh, I guess I didn't say this on air.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它过去是，现在也是，但我曾经瞎搞过各种……你知道的，就像我说的，打印命令——哦，我猜我之前没在节目里说过这个。

sentences.en: So it's like, you know, my first program, I remember, it's like 10, print Patrick rules, 20, go to 10, execute, right?
sentences.zh: 所以就像，你知道的，我的第一个程序，我记得是这样的：10，打印“帕特里克最牛逼”，20，跳转到10，运行，对吧？

sentences.en: And then Patrick rules, Patrick rules, Patrick rules, Patrick rules, Patrick rules, Patrick rules, like all the way down.
sentences.zh: 然后屏幕上就会一路刷下来：“帕特里克最牛逼，帕特里克最牛逼，帕特里克最牛逼……”铺满整屏。

sentences.en: And then, like, you're like calling your brother, hey, look, man, the computer knows I rules.
sentences.zh: 然后你会跑去叫你弟弟：“嘿，你看，电脑知道我很牛逼。”

sentences.en: We would have this arms race.
sentences.zh: 我们过去常搞这种军备竞赛。

sentences.en: So my cousins were all kind of techies, and most of them were older than me.
sentences.zh: 我的表兄弟们都挺懂技术的，而且大部分都比我大。

sentences.en: And so we all had, like, the Commodore 64 manual, and we used this as sort of a way to sort of, like, see who the alpha programmer was at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们都有康道尔64（Commodore 64）的说明书，我们把它当作一种方式，来看看谁才是当时的技术大佬。

sentences.en: So, you know, someone started with the, you know, 10, print, you know, Lynn rules, 20, go to 10.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，有人先写了“10，打印，琳恩最牛逼，20，跳转到10”。

sentences.en: And my cousin was like, check it out, you know.
sentences.zh: 然后我表哥就说：“快看这个。”

sentences.en: And then I figured out a way to, like, print mine so that it, like, moved, it, like, kind of bounced left and right on the bottom of the screen.
sentences.zh: 接着我琢磨出了一种方法，可以让我的名字打印出来时会移动，就像在屏幕底部左右弹跳一样。

sentences.en: Because, like, it'd just go back to 10, but it'd put a bunch of spaces in front.
sentences.zh: 因为，虽然它只是跳回第10行，但在前面加了一堆空格。

sentences.en: And so it looked like it was kind of bouncing.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来它就像是在弹跳一样。

sentences.en: And then, like, another one of my cousins found out you could actually write to specific places on the screen.
sentences.zh: 然后我的另一个表姐发现，你实际上可以把文字写到屏幕上的特定位置。

sentences.en: Like, you could say, I want, like, this row and column to have, like, a letter in it.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以指定：“我想让某一行某一列显示一个字母。”

sentences.en: And so she actually made her name, like, bounce, like, as if it was a little pong ball or something.
sentences.zh: 于是她真的让自己的名字弹跳起来，就像是一个微型的乓球游戏或者别的什么一样。

sentences.en: Ah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 啊，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was super fun.
sentences.zh: 对，超好玩的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, but that kind of encouraging that kind of fun experimentation is really a good way to learn.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，鼓励这种有趣的尝试真的是一种很好的学习方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全同意。

sentences.en: You know, it takes, it's still another leap to go to programming as a, you know, getting things done kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要真正跨入以编程为手段去“搞定事情”的门槛，这仍然需要又一次的飞跃。

sentences.en: But those early lessons are valuable.
sentences.zh: 但那些早期的经验是非常宝贵的。

sentences.en: And the fact that it's so approachable basic was for kids.
sentences.zh: 而且它对孩子们来说非常平易近人，BASIC就是这样。

sentences.en: Like, it's easy to get started in.
sentences.zh: 上手非常容易。

sentences.en: And even though you might move on to other stuff, those early lessons, you know, about, you know, oh, I want to move.
sentences.zh: 即便你后来可能会转向其他东西，但那些早期的经验，你知道的，关于“哦，我想移动……”

sentences.en: But then I want to go back at some time.
sentences.zh: “但我又想在某个时候返回。”

sentences.en: So I need some sort of loop that's counting.
sentences.zh: “所以我需要某种能够计数的循环。”

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You're introducing kind of, even if you don't know it, you're learning these four loops.
sentences.zh: 你其实已经在不知不觉中开始接触和了解循环（for loops）了。

sentences.en: And then later, when you learn the proper concepts, you can map them back to those early things that you were doing.
sentences.zh: 然后等你以后学到了正规的概念，你就能把它们和早期做过的事情对应起来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I noticed that, like, I've taken a lot of different classes and things, like, just on the web.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我注意到，我上过很多不同的课，学过很多东西，比如就在网上。

sentences.en: Like, I recently took Rails for zombies.
sentences.zh: 像我最近上了《僵尸学Rails》（Rails for zombies）。

sentences.en: Have you seen this class?
sentences.zh: 你看过这门课吗？

sentences.en: Ah, I have seen that one.
sentences.zh: 啊，我看过那个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I took this class.
sentences.zh: 我上了这门课。

sentences.en: And pretty much nothing stuck.
sentences.zh: 结果基本上什么都没记住。

sentences.en: Now you're a zombie.
sentences.zh: 现在你成僵尸了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Brains.
sentences.zh: 脑子……

sentences.en: Rails.
sentences.zh: Rails……

sentences.en: So nothing stuck.
sentences.zh: 所以什么都没留下。

sentences.en: And, like, when I went to make a, I recently made a website in Rails.
sentences.zh: 然后，当我想要去制作一个……我最近用Rails做了一个网站。

sentences.en: I forgot everything.
sentences.zh: 我把一切都忘光了。

sentences.en: Like, everything I had to go back and relearn.
sentences.zh: 就像所有东西我都得重新回去学一遍。

sentences.en: And the thing is, when you are, like, when you have a vision in mind, whether it's printing your name over and over again or making a website or whatever,
sentences.zh: 关键是，当你心中有一个愿景时——无论是反复打印你的名字还是做一个网站，不管是什么——

sentences.en: and you're learning something as part of fulfilling that vision, that's when it seems to stick.
sentences.zh: 而且你是在为了实现这个愿景的过程中去学习某些东西，那才是真正能记住的时候。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's so much more effective than trying to learn something through a class or something like that.
sentences.zh: 这比试图通过上课或者类似的方式去硬学要有效率得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: And basically gives you the ability, it's easy enough where you can start with zero.
sentences.zh: BASIC确实赋予了你这种能力，它足够简单，让你能从零开始。

sentences.en: You know, like, you can start not knowing anything about programming and just have, like, a vision of, oh, I want to make, like,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以完全不懂任何编程知识，仅仅怀揣着一个愿景，比如“我想让一个小点在屏幕上移动”或者诸如此类的想法。

sentences.en: a little dot move around the screen or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你不能一开始就抱有太大的目标，不能说“我想做个《雷神之锤》（Quake）”之类的。

sentences.en: I mean, you can't have a huge, you can't say I want to make, you know, Quake or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我刚才正想着《雷神之锤》呢。

sentences.en: I was just thinking Quake.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's awesome.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，像《我的世界》（Minecraft）之类的。

sentences.en: Or, you know, Minecraft or something.
sentences.zh: 或者《矮人要塞》（Dwarf Fortress）。

sentences.en: Or Fortress.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 也许，其实这也不是完全不可能。

sentences.en: Maybe, actually, that might not be out of bounds.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样。

sentences.en: But anyways.
sentences.zh: 总之，如果你有那本书的话，显然你就能做到。

sentences.en: Anyways, so if you have the book, apparently, you can do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，对，我的意思是，如果你有一个简单的愿景，你可以从一无所有开始。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I mean, but, you know, if you have, like, a simple vision, you can start with nothing.
sentences.zh: 直接开始敲BASIC代码，每当遇到不会的东西，就去网上查，然后一步步摸索过去。

sentences.en: Just start typing in BASIC, and every time you can't do something, you look it up on the Internet and get your way through it.
sentences.zh: 那将是一次极其充实的学习体验。

sentences.en: And it will be just an incredibly fulfilling learning experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种程度上讲，我想作为程序员，你最终会告别BASIC。

sentences.en: So, I mean, in some ways, I guess, as programmers, you move on from BASIC.
sentences.zh: 但是，有很多很多人能找到薪酬丰厚的工作，你知道的，仅仅靠编写那些基本上属于BASIC风格的代码。

sentences.en: But, I mean, there are a lot of people who get valuable paying jobs, you know, just writing, you know, essentially basic style things.
sentences.zh: 那也很棒。

sentences.en: And that's great.
sentences.zh: 而且令人惊叹的是，一门诞生于这么久以前的语言居然至今还能存留下来。

sentences.en: And it is amazing that something that was written so long ago kind of still sticks around.
sentences.zh: 即便它不像以前那样至关重要了，你知道的，它依然伴随着我们。

sentences.en: Even if it's not vitally important like it once was, you know, it's still with us.
sentences.zh: 就像我们对它都有美好的回忆一样。

sentences.en: Like, we all have fond memories of it.
sentences.zh: 你依然能找到各种内容——我们稍后会聊到，比如在网上或者其他地方。

sentences.en: There's still, you know, things you can find we'll talk about later, like on the Internet or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你总能找到它的免费版本，而且一直在更新。

sentences.en: You can just find versions of it free that keep being updated.
sentences.zh: 显然，每一个版本的Windows过去都自带了一个版本的BASIC。

sentences.en: And every version of Windows apparently was shipping with a version of BASIC.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这里有一个——所以有一个叫VBA的东西，也就是Visual Basic for Applications。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a – so there's VBA, which is Visual Basic for Applications.
sentences.zh: 它最初其实只是，我猜，叫BA。

sentences.en: And it actually started off as just, I guess, BA.
sentences.zh: 但在早期，也就是Excel的非常早期的版本里。

sentences.en: But, like, in earlier, really early versions of Excel and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 你只需要编写BASIC代码来操作单元格之类的东西。

sentences.en: And you would just write BASIC to, you know, manipulate the cells and things like that.
sentences.zh: 正如帕特里克所说，直到今天依然有人在这么做。

sentences.en: And there's people who, as Patrick said, just do this even to this day.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，按照传统，我们通常会讨论优缺点。

sentences.en: I mean, so we traditionally go through, like, strengths and weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 当然我们也可以这么做。

sentences.en: I mean, we can do that.
sentences.zh: 不过对于这个话题来说，感觉有点怪。

sentences.en: It's a little strange for this one.
sentences.zh: 但我只是觉得——正如杰森所说，坐下来面对一行空白代码，然后让某些事情发生，是如此轻而易举。

sentences.en: But I just think it's so – like Jason said, it's so easy to sit down with essentially a bling line and get something to happen.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有成就感。

sentences.en: And that's really rewarding.
sentences.zh: 耶，我让电脑干了点事，对吧？

sentences.en: Yay, I made the computer do something, right?
sentences.zh: 就像是我给它编写了程序一样。

sentences.en: Like, I programmed it.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: And that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 部分原因要归功于它平易近人的语法。

sentences.en: And that's in part due to the approachable syntax.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它读起来确实很像日常语言。

sentences.en: I mean, it does read a lot.
sentences.zh: 就像我们说的，比起printf或cl，它直接就是print、go to、if，对吧？

sentences.en: Like we said, instead of, like, printf or cl, it's, like, print, go to, if, right?
sentences.zh: 这些东西在某种程度上更容易理解，并且更贴近人们在日常交流中习惯的方式。

sentences.en: I mean, these things are somewhat more understandable and closer to what people know already in their, you know, normal way of communicating.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And something that I just remembered, when I was in college, there was this guy who was going crazy over Dark BASIC.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我刚刚想起来，我上大学时，有个家伙对Dark BASIC（黑暗BASIC）痴迷得不得了。

sentences.en: Dark?
sentences.zh: Dark？

sentences.en: Is that like the vampire BASIC?
sentences.zh: 那是什么，吸血鬼版的BASIC吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's sort of like Rails for Zombies.
sentences.zh: 有点像僵尸版的Rails。

sentences.en: Oh!
sentences.zh: 噢！

sentences.en: That was a lot in common.
sentences.zh: 那确实有很多共同点。

sentences.en: But, so, Dark BASIC is, I think it's commercial.
sentences.zh: 不过，所以，Dark BASIC它，我觉得它是商业软件。

sentences.en: Let me see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: You write games in this.
sentences.zh: 你用这个来写游戏。

sentences.en: I think I do remember this.
sentences.zh: 我想我确实还记得这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I actually allow you to do, like, graphics programming and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，它其实允许你做一些图形编程之类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if it's free or not.
sentences.zh: 我不确定它是不是免费的。

sentences.en: But, basically, it's a way to get access to DirectX, which is Microsoft's, like, rendering library, like, a rendering platform.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，它是一种访问DirectX的方式，DirectX是微软的渲染库，也就是一个渲染平台。

sentences.en: And, so, you can write basic programs, but instead of just kind of printing your name and doing cheesy things that we were talking about, you could actually, like, create, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以编写基础的程序，但不仅仅是打印你的名字或者做我们刚才说的那些无聊的事情，你实际上可以，比如，创建，像

sentences.en: little sprites.
sentences.zh: 小精灵。

sentences.en: You could load images and have them, like, move around.
sentences.zh: 你可以加载图像并让它们四处移动。

sentences.en: And, so, for people out there, like, budding game designers and people who want to sort of, like, write a game really quick but have no experience in programming,
sentences.zh: 所以，对大家来说，比如有志于成为游戏设计的人，以及那些想快速编写游戏但又没有任何编程经验的人，

sentences.en: you should definitely check out Dark BASIC.
sentences.zh: 你们绝对应该去了解一下Dark BASIC。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I remember, I mean, those were the first games I wrote.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我是说，那些是我写的第一批游戏。

sentences.en: Not that I've written many games, but, you know, something like you were talking about.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说我写过很多游戏，但你知道的，就像你刚才说的那种。

sentences.en: But, I actually, like, there was a way to draw to the screen, and so, I would learn about, like,
sentences.zh: 不过，实际上，我有办法在屏幕上绘图，所以，我会学习关于，比如

sentences.en: erasing the screen and then drawing a little square and making it bounce off the corners and learn about flipping the velocities, right?
sentences.zh: 擦除屏幕然后画一个小方块，让它在角落里弹来弹去，并了解如何翻转速度，对吧？

sentences.en: Which I didn't know it was a term, but, like, oh, I need to move five pixels to the right.
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道这叫什么术语，但就是，哦，我需要向右移动五个像素。

sentences.en: But, when I hit the screen, I need to know where the screen's at, and then I need to make that negative and move plus minus five pixels, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，当我碰到屏幕边缘时，我需要知道屏幕在哪里，然后我需要把它变成负数并移动正负五个像素，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, like, learning how, like, that's how that works and figuring it out and that sense of triumph you have.
sentences.zh: 还有，比如了解它是如何工作的，自己琢磨出来，那种油然而生的成就感。

sentences.en: And then, also, I may, like, try to make, like, a little Pac-Man thing where the mouth would open and close.
sentences.zh: 然后，我还可能会试着做一个类似吃豆人的东西，它的嘴巴会一张一合。

sentences.en: Oh, nice.
sentences.zh: 噢，不错。

sentences.en: Instead of using, which, later learning, they have sprites to do that, right?
sentences.zh: 而不是使用，后来才知道，他们有专门的精灵来实现那个功能，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, just various animation.
sentences.zh: 就像各种动画一样。

sentences.en: I would actually draw, like, a pie circle, like, with the angle, and then the angle would get smaller and bigger, right?
sentences.zh: 我实际上会画一个扇形，带角度的那种，然后角度会变小变大，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, that's awesome.
sentences.zh: 噢，那太棒了。

sentences.en: And it would kind of go across, and, you know, you don't know any difference, so you just make do.
sentences.zh: 而且它会从屏幕上滑过去，而且，你知道的，你什么都不懂，所以只能将就着来。

sentences.en: So, this is kind of, like, a little segue here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这算是一个小小的过渡。

sentences.en: But, they, I was reading this really interesting article on, I've been doing a lot of drawing lately, as, you know, I mentioned a while ago, maybe in an earlier episode.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们，我当时在读一篇非常有趣的文章关于，我最近一直在画画，正如，你知道的，我前段时间提到过，可能是在之前的某一集里。

sentences.en: And I have one of those Wacom tablets, those USB drawing tablets.
sentences.zh: 而且我有一个Wacom数位板，那种USB绘图板。

sentences.en: And I've been reading a lot of books and papers on drawing, as well.
sentences.zh: 我也一直在阅读大量关于绘画的书籍和论文。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I thought was just fascinating, and I didn't believe it until I actually saw examples of it, is if you have two frames.
sentences.zh: 其中有一件事我觉得非常神奇，而且在我亲眼看到实例之前我是不相信的，那就是如果你有两帧画面。

sentences.en: So, imagine, like, you have one frame where Pac-Man's mouth is open, and another frame where his mouth is closed.
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下，比如你有一帧是吃豆人张开嘴巴，另一帧是它的嘴巴闭上。

sentences.en: And you just, like, flip-flop between these two frames.
sentences.zh: 而你只是在这两帧之间来回切换。

sentences.en: It will look, like, weird and cheesy, and it won't look right.
sentences.zh: 这看起来会很怪异、很生硬，而且感觉不对劲。

sentences.en: But if you have three frames, or I guess in this case five frames, so you have, like, mouth open, halfway closed, closed, halfway closed, open.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有三帧，或者我想在这个例子里是五帧，也就是你有：嘴巴张开、半闭、闭合、半闭、张开。

sentences.en: Like, if you just add that third frame, there's something in your brain where your brain can't remember three frames back, and it looks like fluid motion.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你加上第三帧，你的大脑里就会产生一种机制，让你记不住三帧之前的情景，然后它看起来就像是流畅的动作。

sentences.en: Like, this sounds crazy, but if you just Google that or something, or maybe I'll post a link on the blog.

sentences.en: It'll never be, like, high-performing.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会有很高的性能。

sentences.en: The other thing is it doesn't have a lot of the bells and whistles that would make your life easy as a developer.

sentences.en: It doesn't have object-oriented paradigm.
sentences.zh: 它没有面向对象的范式。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's not going to let you make that killer app.

sentences.zh: 绝对充满活力。

sentences.zh: 然后是工具，正如我们所说，市面上有很多FreeBASIC的版本。

sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我所发现的，要搜索BASIC真的很难，因为当你搜BASIC编程时，结果出来的往往只是编程入门教程。

sentences.en: It's like, no, I want BASIC programming, not simple programming.
sentences.zh: 就好像在说：不，我要找的是BASIC编程，而不是简单的编程。

sentences.en: So it is a little hard to search for.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实有点难搜。

sentences.en: And there are many, like, web-based versions for the interpreters to download.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多基于网络的解释器版本可供下载。

sentences.en: And it's still a great thing to start today.
sentences.zh: 现在开始学习它依然是个很棒的选择。

sentences.en: I think if you have kids or you do one day, I think it would be a great way to introduce them, you know, to programming.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你有孩子或者将来有的话，这会是向他们介绍编程的一个绝佳途径。

sentences.en: And this is, like I said, this is how my earliest programming was done in BASIC.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我最早的编程就是用BASIC完成的。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 我们当时就是在计算器上干这个。

sentences.en: And, you know, it started off, like, you know, a math class.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，最开始，是在数学课上。

sentences.en: Our teacher would say, like, oh, you know, you couldn't, like, eventually there was a way to, like, download from the Internet.
sentences.zh: 我们的老师会说，哦，你知道的，你不能，后来不知怎么出现了一种可以通过互联网下载的方法。

sentences.en: You could download programs and run them.
sentences.zh: 你可以下载程序并运行它们。

sentences.en: But if you could, like, program something yourself, like, you could use it for, like, geometry to compute the hypotenuse of a triangle, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能自己编写程序，比如你可以把它用在几何课上计算三角形的斜边，对吧？

sentences.en: So we, like, code in simple formulas into our calculators.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在计算器里写一些简单的公式代码。

sentences.en: And then eventually, yeah, like, I wrote, like, both of us turned out, we wrote, like, a little RPG.
sentences.zh: 然后慢慢地，是的，我和你都写过那种小型的RPG游戏。

sentences.en: You know, it was, like, a little turn-based fighting game where you were, it was generating random numbers and deciding if you would hit the guy or not.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是一个小型回合制格斗游戏，它会生成随机数来决定你是否能击中对方。

sentences.en: And you did, like, really simple things.
sentences.zh: 你做的都是非常简单的东西。

sentences.en: But, you know, you learned a lot.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你学到了很多。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the other thing is we had this awesome arms race in our math class.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，另一件趣事是我们的数学课上曾有过一场精彩的军备竞赛。

sentences.en: So, for example, we started writing programs to solve a lot of the geometry probleMs.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们开始编写程序来解决许多几何问题。

sentences.en: And then the teacher, she caught on to it.
sentences.zh: 然后老师发现了这一点。

sentences.en: And she was cool with us writing the prograMs.
sentences.zh: 她对我们写程序这件事其实挺开明的。

sentences.en: The problem is that they were getting into the hands of, like, all the students in the class.
sentences.zh: 问题是这些程序开始流传到班里所有学生的手中。

sentences.en: And some students, like, were just using the program.
sentences.zh: 有些学生只是直接使用这个程序。

sentences.en: They didn't really know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道代码里是怎么回事。

sentences.en: They were just putting in the answer.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把答案输进去。

sentences.en: So, she decided that she's going to, like, make you wipe your calculator.
sentences.zh: 所以，她决定要强制清空大家的计算器。

sentences.en: But I didn't want my calculator to get wiped because I had all these games on it that I was working on, right?
sentences.zh: 但我不想让我的计算器被清空，因为上面有我正在编写的各种游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: So, I wrote a program that looked like the wipe your calculator screen.
sentences.zh: 于是我写了一个程序，看起来就像是清空计算器的屏幕界面。

sentences.en: But when you hit it, it didn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 但当你点击它时，什么都不会发生。

sentences.en: And then, like, and then, you know, when you're in, like, middle school or high school, you want to be cool.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，当你在初中或高中时，你总想表现得很酷。

sentences.en: So, I started showing it off and other people started writing it.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始炫耀它，其他人也开始跟着写。

sentences.en: So, then we all had the program.
sentences.zh: 于是我们所有人都有了这个程序。

sentences.en: Then the teacher found out about the program.
sentences.zh: 接着老师发现了这个程序的存在。

sentences.en: And so, we ended up with this arms race of, like, could you keep your stuff on the calculator?
sentences.zh: 结果我们陷入了一场军备竞赛：看你能不能把自己的东西保存在计算器里？

sentences.en: That's horrible.
sentences.zh: 太惨了。

sentences.zh: 对，我们没有经历过那个。

sentences.zh: 但我们班确实有人，老师会允许，也许是个女老师，我现在记不清了，会允许使用程序。

sentences.en: But they wouldn't actually write prograMs.

sentences.en: They didn't know how or didn't care to learn.

sentences.zh: 而我可不想惹上大麻烦或者失去使用计算器的资格。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I just wouldn't share it at all because I wanted to be able to use it.
